- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) or negative (0.00), model underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if price is trending up.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after rising), model often fails to recognize it — add a “reversion buffer” to forecast: if price > 20% above 10-day moving average, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overfits recent trends — especially when sentiment is volatile — apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule: if sentiment swings >0.33, reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- If true outcome is below 70% of 30-day average, model often underestimates — adjust forecast to align with 10–15% above historical low if sentiment is neutral or negative.
